text:
incident-bot: 🚨 ALERT: autoscaler reported capacity exhaustion in us-west-2 (gpu-pool-4). queue_length=~12k, scale_attempts=5, throttled_requests=high. Link: https://console.redwood/inference/alerts/1765009876

maya_oncall: picking this up — oncall for infra. seeing 500s in the api. trying to get a quick summary: who owns the pool?

sanjay: gpu-pool-4 is a mixed-MIG pool (8g/4g slices) used by hosted tier + a few dedicated slices. recent deploy increased 2x BATCH jobs. autoscaler hit node limit and timed out.

ops-runner: logs from the scaler: 
```
E0315 09:12:09 scaler.go:412] scale attempt failed: insufficient binpackable capacity: available_slices=22 required_slices=48
E0315 09:12:09 scheduler.go:287] placement failed: fragmentation prevents allocation for req=1xA100-80GB or 2xA100-40GB
```

maya_oncall: so fragmentation + MIG sizing mismatch. is there stranded capacity? can we evict anything?

katie: Customer impact: several production customers on hosted API seeing slowdowns and intermittent 503s. Support already opened two tickets. Impact score: P1 for one customer (high QPS).

chen: Metrics: queue growth started ~09:05 UTC. token-throughput dropped by 60%. Node utilization shows a lot of isolated free GPUs but cannot be packed due to small MIG slices + pinned pods.

maya_oncall: deploy a quick mitigation plan: 1) pause non-critical batch jobs 2) open manual scale to bring up spare homogeneous nodes (no MIG) 3) consider temporary reconfigure to coarser MIG or full GPU for critical routes. Thoughts?

sanjay: agree. pausing batch jobs now. I pushed a label change to batch jobs to prevent new scheduling: `kubectl label workloads batch=true paused=true --selector=env=prod`

incident-bot: runbook suggestion: "GPU fragmentation mitigation" (https://runbooks.redwood/frag-mitigation). Recommended: manual drain of low-util pods, create temporary dedicated pool, and force-schedule critical traffic there.

runbook-bot: runbook steps applied check: pause noncritical=true, create temp-pool suggested_command: `redwoodctl pool create --name temp-rt --machine-type a100-80g --count 6 --region us-west-2`

ops-runner: starting pool create now. submitting API to cloudprovider — estimate 6-8 mins for node readiness.

katie: notify affected customers with ETA ~15min. I'll draft the message.

maya_oncall: manual rebalance options while we wait: - evict pinned low-priority pods from mixed pool - cordon nodes with fragmented slices and force new nodes to use full GPU instances - attempt MIG reconfiguration (risky)

chen: MIG reconfiguration requires node reboot and takes ~10-12 mins per node, I'd avoid unless necessary. binpack-first scheduling could help but scheduler currently can't fit because requests ask for contiguous slices.

sanjay: started eviction for noncritical pods. command: `kubectl drain gpu-node-57 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force` (doing one node at a time).

ops-runner: temp-rt pool created (6 a100-80g nodes). Adding to routing as dedicated overflow for critical routes. updating router policies now.

maya_oncall: routing change: route /v1/generate-critical -> temp-rt pool. applying canary 10% then 50%.

incident-bot: update: 09:34 UTC autoscaler still failing on original pool, but temp-rt accepted traffic. queue length trending down (12k -> 3.1k).

katie: customer notification sent: "We're routing critical requests to a dedicated overflow pool; latency should improve in ~10 minutes. We're investigating root cause and will follow up." :white_check_mark:

chen: observed some stranded slices on nodes with many small MIGs reserved by long-lived pods. looks like older deployments pinned model shards to 4g slices. need a cleanup plan post-incident.

maya_oncall: agree this is recurring pattern. immediate: keep temp-rt until we rebalance. medium: change autoscaler to be more permissive with fallback to full-gpu variants. long-term: plan for model packing/quantization guidance to reduce slice requests.

sanjay: adding a short-term autoscaler tweak: increase max_nodes for gpu-pool-4 by +12 to avoid hitting scale limit. applied: `kubectl patch hpa autoscaler-gpu-pool-4 -p '{"spec":{"maxReplicas":80}}'`

ops-runner: after scale tweak and evictions, queue is ~900 and token throughput at 80% of baseline. throttled requests dropping.

incident-bot: Incident timeline summary (auto): 09:05 queue growth; 09:12 autoscaler failures due to fragmentation/binpack; 09:20 paused batch jobs; 09:28 created temp-rt; 09:34 routing partial; 09:40 queue decreasing.

katie: prepping postmortem notifications and customer follow-ups. recommended severity: Sev2 (multiple customers impacted but mitigated within 40min).

chen: follow-up items I’ll own: 1) inventory pinned MIG workloads + owners 2) design migration strategy to coarser MIGs or full GPUs 3) scheduler improvement: allow best-effort allocation to use multiple small slices rather than requiring contiguous pack.

maya_oncall: handoff to oncall-next: @sanjay will be oncall for the next shift — make sure temp-rt remains for at least 2 hours and do not revert autoscaler max without validating.

sanjay: taking handoff. I'll monitor for 1h then start a controlled rollback of temp routing if metrics stable.

ops-runner: final ops note: created a ticket INF-4292 to track stranded capacity cleanup and autoscaler tuning.

katie: adding customer follow-up timeline and inc-comms doc.

maya_oncall: thanks team. Incident resolved for now; continuing monitoring. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Channel will remain open for updates."
